plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective drawing of a toroid with a rectangular cross-section, cut open so the reader faces the flat end of the ring. The gray body carries fine radial hatching across its curved upper surface, and the central hole opens through the middle. Across the top, four horizontal dimension arrows stack in registration with a dashed vertical center line: the longest reaches the outer wall and is labeled R2, the next reaches the inner wall and is labeled R1, a third labeled r ends partway out, and a short one labeled dr marks a narrow increment just beyond it. At the right edge a vertical bracket labeled h gives the height of the rectangular face. Inside that face, at radius r, a thin vertical strip of width dr is filled solid orange and tagged da by a curved leader. A red arrow labeled i curls onto the left end of the ring, and two blue curved arrows sweep along the lower body in the direction of the circulating field. Setting one narrow shaded strip against the full cross-section signals that the flux is built up by integrating such elements outward from R1 to R2, which is what the self-inductance calculation requires.

elements: toroid body: a rectangular-cross-section ring (annular box extruded around the vertical axis) with the front half cut away so the reader looks into the flat rectangular end faces
fine radial hatching lines across the curved upper surface of the toroid
central cylindrical hole through the middle
rectangular cross-section face on the right cut end, width R2−R1 and height h
thin vertical orange strip of width dr at radius r on the right cross-section face, labeled da
dashed vertical center line rising above the toroid
four stacked horizontal dimension arrows: R2 to outer wall, R1 to inner wall, r to the orange strip, dr marking the strip width
vertical dimension bracket labeled h giving the cross-section height at the right
red curved arrow labeled i curling onto the left end of the ring (current entering the winding)
two blue curved arrows along the lower body indicating the circulating magnetic field direction

interactions.label: radius r
interactions.teaches: Dragging the orange da strip from R1 toward R2 moves it across the rectangular cross-section while B(r) = μ₀NI/(2πr) and dΦ = B(r)·h·dr update — the learner sees the field weaken as 1/r, so equal-width slices at larger radius contribute less flux

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching from one highlighted dr strip to the filled region swept from R1 to the current r reveals the flux linkage as the sum of dΦ contributions, building toward the total Φ = (μ₀NIh/2π)·ln(R2/R1) used in the self-inductance calculation

demo_steps.title: A single slice near the inner wall
demo_steps.narration: With the orange da strip near R1, B(r) is strongest and dΦ = B·h·dr is relatively large. Read the live values of B and dΦ beside the figure.

demo_steps.title: Drag the slice outward
demo_steps.narration: Move r toward R2. The strip crosses the cross-section and dΦ shrinks as 1/r — outer slices contribute less flux per unit width.

demo_steps.title: Sum the slices
demo_steps.narration: Switch to Accumulated integral: the region from R1 to r fills in, showing the partial flux Φ(r). Sweep r outward again to watch the total build toward μ₀NIh·ln(R2/R1)/(2π).

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Toroid centered at origin with vertical symmetry axis (Y up). Inner radius R1 = 1.0, outer radius R2 = 2.1 world units; cross-section height h = 0.7, so the body occupies y ∈ [−0.35, 0.35]. Render the full ring minus a front wedge of ~120° (azimuth ±60° about the camera-facing direction) so both rectangular cut faces are visible; the right cut face lies roughly in the X–Y plane at screen-right and carries the orange strip. Orange strip: thin box of radial width dr = 0.08 and full height h, positioned at radius r on the right face, color #e8701a; in Accumulated mode, an orange annular-sector slab fills R1→r at 40% opacity on top of the face. Body gray #9aa0a6 with darker hatching strokes #555 on the curved top surface. Dimension arrows black, above the toroid: R2 arrow at top spanning center-line to r=2.1, R1 to r=1.0, r arrow ending at the strip, dr short double-arrow beside the strip; dashed gray vertical line through the axis and dashed verticals dropping from arrow ends. h bracket vertical at far right of the face. Red current arrow #cc2222 at the left end face; two blue field arrows #2277cc sweeping along the lower body tangentially. Physics: B(r) = μ₀NI/(2πr) with N·I set so B(R1)=1 in arbitrary units; dΦ = B·h·dr; total Φ(r) = (μ₀NIh/2π)·ln(r/R1), full Φ = that with r=R2.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the toroid as a LatheGeometry/extruded annular sector so the cut wedge is native; the rectangular end faces need flat shading to read as the cross-section. Move the orange strip and update the r/dr arrows, the B(r) and dΦ numeric readouts, and the accumulated fill geometry reactively on every slider change. Keep all four dimension arrows in vertical registration with the dashed center line as in the source. Hatching can be a static set of radial line segments on the top surface — it does not need to respond to interactions.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a perspective drawing of a toroid with a rectangular cross-section, cut open so the reader faces the flat end of the ring. The gray body carries fine radial hatching across its curved upper surface, and the central hole opens through the middle. Across the top, four horizontal dimension arrows stack in registration with a dashed vertical center line: the longest reaches the outer wall and is labeled R2, the next reaches the inner wall and is labeled R1, a third labeled r ends partway out, and a short one labeled dr marks a narrow increment just beyond it. At the right edge a vertical bracket labeled h gives the height of the rectangular face. Inside that face, at radius r, a thin vertical strip of width dr is filled solid orange and tagged da by a curved leader. A red arrow labeled i curls onto the left end of the ring, and two blue curved arrows sweep along the lower body in the direction of the circulating field. Setting one narrow shaded strip against the full cross-section signals that the flux is built up by integrating such elements outward from R1 to R2, which is what the self-inductance calculation requires.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radius r: the learner drags the orange da strip from R1 toward R2, the strip moves across the rectangular cross-section while B(r) and dPhi values update, showing why each radial slice contributes a different amount of flux.
- Toggle between single slice and accumulated integral: the learner switches from one highlighted dr strip to the filled region swept from R1 to the current r, revealing how summing dPhi over radius builds the toroid's total flux linkage.
